info.title: AgentConnect API
info.description: The C2 BFF REST surface (Web UI ⇄ Control Plane). Every resource is org-scoped under `/api/v1/orgs/:orgId` behind bearer auth; a cross-org id reads as 404. The Control Plane stores only control-plane metadata — message bodies and workspace bytes stay daemon-local.

get.description: Every organization the caller belongs to, with their role. Self-heals an interrupted signup by (re)creating the caller’s personal org.

post.description: Create an organization; the caller becomes its first owner. A slug collision returns 409.

get.description: The signed-in user's own profile: identity, display name, and avatar.

patch.description: Edit your display name. Email remains managed by the sign-in provider; profile photos use the dedicated upload endpoint.

get.description: Your active personal API keys across every organization you belong to, never exposing the secret or its hash.

post.description: Mints a personal API key in one of your organizations (default 90-day expiry; pass `expiresInDays: null` for a non-expiring key). The key acts as you, with your role in that org. The plaintext is returned exactly once and is never retrievable afterward.

delete.description: Revokes one of your own API keys as a kill switch; the next request presenting it is rejected. A key id that isn’t yours reads as absent (404).

post.description: Redeems a valid link for the signed-in account as collaborator. A removed account cannot redeem the same link again.

get.description: The organization from the caller’s perspective (id, name, slug, their role, member count).

patch.description: Rename or re-slug the organization (owner only). A slug collision returns 409.

delete.description: Delete the organization (owner only). Refused with 409 while it still has daemons. If a GitHub Check may already exist, the first DELETE permanently tombstones and disables the current hook lifecycles, starts asynchronous non-passing cleanup, and returns 409; retry DELETE after cleanup converges to complete the metadata purge and cascade.

get.description: The org’s daemon fleet from the registry, each overlaid with its live connection status (a daemon that has exited reads as offline).

patch.description: Assign a human-friendly console display name to a daemon.

delete.description: Remove a daemon from the fleet, cascading its keys, leases, and launches; refused while it is online and reachable.

post.description: Provision a new daemon (a provisioned row plus its first API key) and return a ready-to-run connect command for onboarding.

put.description: Set the daemon’s visibility (org-wide vs restricted) and share set. Requires edit rights on the daemon; sharedWith is intersected with current org members.

get.description: Lists a daemon’s API keys, never exposing the secret or its hash.

post.description: Mints an additional API key for an existing daemon (overlap rotation or "Regenerate"), returning the one-time plaintext and a ready-to-run start command.

delete.description: Revokes one of a daemon’s API keys as a kill switch; a key from another daemon or org reads as absent (404).

post.description: Mint a new agent definition scoped to the caller’s org; the CP assigns its UUID. With ?connect=true, also provisions a daemon connect token and start command for onboarding.

get.description: Every agent definition in the caller’s active org.
Fetch one agent by id; a cross-org id reads as absent (404).

patch.description: Edit the agent spec or widen an existing GitHub workspace from read to write access; the change hot-syncs the owning daemon’s replica and rides the next register/launch.

delete.description: Remove the agent definition and its hooks, then tell the owning daemon to drop it from its local replica (best-effort).

put.summary: Convert a scratch workspace to GitHub
put.description: Promote an empty scratch workspace to an explicitly authorized GitHub repository. The owning daemon drains active work, clones the repository, and acknowledges activation; agent configuration, integrations, sessions, and memory are preserved.

put.summary: Move an agent to another daemon
put.description: Cold-reprovision an agent on another READY daemon. The active turn is drained; daemon-local workspace, memory, and transcript data are not migrated.
Set the agent’s visibility (org-wide vs restricted) and share set. Requires edit rights on the agent; sharedWith is intersected with current org members.
Set which peer agents may call this agent as a sub-agent. Requires edit rights on the target agent; the allow-list is intersected with visible same-org peer agents.

get.description: Proxy one directory page live from the owning daemon; a missing directory is data (exists:false), not an error. 503 when unplaced or the daemon is offline.
Proxy one byte slice of a file live from the owning daemon (64 KiB default; page with offset while truncated). A missing file is data (exists:false); binary files come back encoding:none.
Proxy the agent's memory index (<agent-root>/memory/MEMORY.md) live from the owning daemon; a not-yet-created file is data (exists:false). 503 when unplaced or the daemon is offline.
List the files in the agent's memory dir (MEMORY.md index + topic files) live from the owning daemon. 503 when unplaced or the daemon is offline.
Proxy one byte slice of a memory file (?path defaults to MEMORY.md) live from the owning daemon; a missing file is data (exists:false). 503 when unplaced or the daemon is offline.

put.description: Replace one memory file (?path defaults to MEMORY.md) on the owning daemon; returns the written size/mtime. `ifMatchMtime` (optional) is optimistic concurrency — a 409 if the file changed under you. Requires edit permission. 503 when unplaced or the daemon is offline.

get.description: Report whether the owning daemon’s checkout is clean; a dirty tree or a from-scratch (non-repo) workspace is data (clean/isRepo), not an error.

post.description: Force an on-demand ff-only pull on the owning daemon; a pull that can’t fast-forward (diverged, local edits) is data (ok:false + detail), only an offline daemon yields 503.

get.description: Explicit GitHub repository grants for this agent. An App-backed workspace repo is implicit and not listed; scratch workspaces may grant any covered repository, while a manual GitHub workspace may explicitly grant only its own repo for review/check effects. Gated by the agent’s visibility.

post.summary: Authorize a repository for an agent
post.description: Grant the agent access to a GitHub repository. App-backed workspaces may add repositories beyond their implicit workspace grant, scratch workspaces may add any covered repository, and a manual GitHub workspace may explicitly authorize only its own repository for control-plane review/check effects. The repository must be covered by one of the organization’s GitHub App installations; with the per-user gate configured, the caller must hold the matching GitHub permission (`read`/`comment` tiers need read, `write` needs write).

patch.description: Raise an existing repository grant to a stronger access tier after re-checking the caller’s matching GitHub permission. Downgrades still require revoke and reauthorize so review-check cleanup remains explicit.

delete.description: Atomically retire existing informational Checks to a non-passing cleanup state and remove the grant. A legacy grant that resolves to the still-authorized workspace repository is removed without retiring its Checks. Already-minted tokens live out their ≤1h expiry (the documented revocation window); the next credential request for a genuinely additional repo is denied.

post.description: Mints a short-lived token the browser presents to the relay pool to start a playground webchat session with this agent. Returns the token, the relay ingress URL, and the conversation id (fresh, or echoed for resume).
Install a platform integration on a placed agent, reusing a free bot or registering a new one from pasted tokens, then push it live to the owning daemon.

get.description: Every platform integration in the active organization, each with its per-channel bindings.

patch.description: Set a channel's trigger (@-mention vs any message), then push the integration's recomputed bindRules to the owning daemon.

delete.description: Delete the integration metadata (the bot and its tokens survive, freed for the next install), then tell the owning daemon to drop it.

get.description: The org's durable platform bot identities, including freed and prebuilt bots offered for reuse.
Fetch a single bot identity by id (scoped to the caller's org; a cross-org id reads as 404).

delete.description: Forget a bot and, via cascade, its stored tokens; refused while the bot is installed on an agent (uninstall the integration first).

patch.description: Toggle the bot's shared-bot opt-in. Enabling moves its inbound onto a relay (many agents may then share it); disabling reverts it to a classic single-agent socket.

post.description: Sync AgentConnect's required configuration into an existing Slack app without deleting user-owned manifest fields, then check the workspace installation's granted bot scopes. Returns Slack settings links when manual permission updates or workspace reinstallation are required.

get.description: Every MCP provider in the active organization (metadata + upstream header names only).

post.description: Register an org-level upstream MCP server (http transport, org visibility) and mint its bearer grant key. The grant key is returned exactly once and is never retrievable afterward; upstream header values go in and never come back.

get.description: Fetch a single MCP provider by id (scoped to the caller's org; a cross-org id reads as 404). Header values and the grant key are never returned.

patch.description: Edit an MCP provider’s url and/or upstream headers. `headers` replaces the stored set wholesale; a changed url passes the SSRF gate. Name, transport, and visibility are immutable through this surface (agents bind by name; recreate to rename).

delete.description: Delete an MCP provider and cascade-drop its upstream secret and grants. (The relay/daemon unbind is wired in a later step.)

post.summary: Rotate an MCP provider grant key
post.description: Mint a fresh bearer grant key for the provider and retire the previous one. The new key + binding are pushed to relays and daemons before the old grant is revoked (grace-safe). Like create, the new grant key is returned exactly once and is never retrievable afterward.

put.description: Set the provider’s visibility (org-wide vs restricted) and share set. Requires edit rights; sharedWith is intersected with current org members.

get.description: The active org’s members — membership joined with each user’s profile.

post.description: Owner-only. Adds a member by email with the given role; no email is sent — an unknown address becomes an invited row, claimed on first SSO sign-in.

patch.description: Owner-only. Changes a member’s role; the last owner can’t be demoted, which would orphan the org.

delete.description: Owner-only. Removes a member from the org; the last owner can’t be removed, which would orphan the org.

get.description: Owner-only. Returns the organization’s single invite-link slot, including expired or revoked state. The plaintext token is never returned.

post.description: Owner-only. Generates the single seven-day, unlimited-use collaborator link. An active link must be revoked or expire first. The token is returned exactly once.

delete.description: Owner-only. Immediately revokes the link. Existing memberships are unchanged.

put.description: Idempotent upsert of a cron definition keyed on its client-minted UUID; every write is best-effort pushed live to the owning agent’s daemon.

get.description: A single cron definition by id, scoped to the caller’s active organization.

delete.description: Remove a cron definition and best-effort push the removal to the owning agent’s daemon.

get.description: Every cron definition in the caller’s active organization.
Daemon-reported run history for a cron, newest first.

post.description: Fire the cron on its daemon immediately; the 202 only means the daemon accepted the fire — the run itself is async and lands in the run history.

put.description: Set the cron’s visibility (org-wide vs restricted) and share set. Requires edit rights on the cron; sharedWith is intersected with current org members.

post.description: Create a trigger for one agent. `kind:"webhook"` mints an ingress URL (the response carries it plus — when requested — the one-time HMAC signing secret, never retrievable again). `kind:"github"` subscribes a repository covered by one of the organization’s GitHub App installations to issue/PR events.

get.description: Every hook firing this agent. Gated by the agent’s visibility.
A single hook definition by id, scoped to the caller’s active organization.

put.description: Update a hook definition. `kind` is immutable (it discriminates the body); a webhook hook’s ingress URL and signing secret are immutable too — rotating either is a delete + re-create. A github hook’s repository may be re-targeted (re-validated against the organization’s installations).

delete.description: Remove a hook definition and drop its rule from the relay pool.

get.description: Delivery/run history for a hook, newest first (metadata only — payloads never reach the CP).
Lists CP-stored session metadata synced by daemon event/session snapshots; transcript bodies remain daemon-local.
Proxies a page of the session's chat history live from the owning daemon (resolved via the row's agentId); 503 if the agent is unplaced or its daemon is offline.

Proxies one byte slice of a tool call's untruncated ToolBody JSON live from the owning daemon; the console pages by offset until nextOffset is null. 503 if the agent is unplaced or its daemon is offline.
Sums the persisted per-session token usage over the selected time window, grouped by agent, plus workspace totals.
Server-sent event feed relaying each converged session milestone (metadata only) for the org’s daemons.
